one_month_reasoning: The main event in the window is the fiscal Q1 2027 (September quarter) report. Lam has not announced the date; aggregators estimate about Oct 21-22, and Lam reported the year-earlier quarter on Oct 22, 2025, so it very likely falls inside the window. The guide was $8.10B +/- $0.4B revenue and $2.15 +/- $0.15 EPS, and Lam beat in the June quarter, so a beat and a higher December guide are likely. Much of that is priced: the stock is about +10% since the Aug 3 close ($294.6) and +29% from the Jul 29 pre-earnings close ($252), and it has already bounced about 20% off the Sep 16-17 closing lows ($269). AI-sentiment shocks moved it hard even on good news (-5.7% on Sep 10 after record results, -8% on Sep 14 on the AI 'pacing' call). Other window events: TSMC and ASML mid-October prints and China export-control headlines. I centre at about $326 (slight post-beat drift and momentum) with a monthly lognormal sigma of 17.5%, up from 16.5% in round 1 because realized volatility since August is 55-73% and three single-day moves of 6-14% have happened since July. The result is close to symmetric.

fair_value.method: 55% forward P/E and 45% FCF yield, 12 months out. P/E: FY28 (June 2028) EPS of $11.9 x 26x = $309. FCF yield: FY28 revenue $41.5B x 31% FCF margin = $12.9B at 3.5%, plus about $3B net cash, over 1.245B shares = $298. Blend about $304, slightly below today's $324.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY2028 EPS $11.9 x 26x forward P/E (in Sep 2027 the stock is valued on NTM EPS, which is mostly FY28)

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 consensus of $9.51 grown about 25%. FY28 (Jul-27 to Jun-28) spans SEMI's July 2026 view of CY27 WFE +21.8% and CY28 +14.1%, so industry growth for the fiscal year is about 18%. Add operating leverage toward the mid-40s operating-margin target and about 1% a year of net buyback. That is 1% above the S&P Global consensus of $11.74. JPM/GS WFE paths (seen via secondary copies) are the upside check only.

Today's forward P/E is about 34x FY27 and 28x FY28. Base rate: in the year into past WFE peaks the multiple collapsed. Year-end trailing P/E went from 15.9x (2017) to 6.8x (2018), from 21.3x (2021) to 11.0x (2022), and from 29.7x (2023) to 21.7x (2024) in the flat-WFE year. That is 27-57% compression, starting 6-12 months before the peak. SEMI forecasts no WFE decline through 2028, but growth slows from +22% to +14%. That second-derivative slowdown is when semicap usually starts to de-rate. So I take about 7% compression from today's FY28 multiple (28x to 26x) in the base case and put the full historical-style de-rating (18x or lower) in the bear case, not the base case.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 revenue $41.5B x 31% FCF margin = $12.9B FCF; 3.5% yield gives $368B; plus about $3B net cash; over 1.245B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 consensus of $34.9B plus about 19%, in line with SEMI's July 2026 WFE growth for the Jul-27 to Jun-28 window (+21.8% CY27, +14.1% CY28). This is trimmed from $42B in round 1, which leaned on JPM/GS secondary copies.

FY26 operating cash flow was $5.86B on $23.2B revenue (about 25%). The margin rises with the long-term framework (GM mid-50s, OM mid-40s). Implied FY28 net income of about $14.8B ($11.9 x 1.245B) at 85-92% conversion gives 30-33%. I take 31%, allowing for capex and working capital to support the cleanroom build-out.
The inverse of about 28x FCF, consistent with a mid-20s forward P/E for a high-conversion business late in the upcycle.
$1.85B at June 2026 ($5.58B cash less $3.73B debt). FCF above the roughly $4B a year of buybacks and dividends adds a little by Sep 2027.
1.256B diluted at Q4 FY26, less about 1% from net buybacks by Sep 2027.

bear.story: By mid-2027 the market starts to price a 2028-29 WFE digestion as growth slows to +14% (SEMI) or turns negative: hyperscaler capex pauses (another AI 'pacing' shock like Sep 14), DRAM/HBM pricing rolls over, or macro weakens. FY28 EPS expectations slip to about $10.5 and the multiple falls to about 18x. That matches the 2018 and 2022 de-ratings (trailing P/E down 48-57%) and the 40-55% drawdowns of past cycles. China rules are a secondary driver, since China is already only 26% of revenue and the MATCH Act was softened before its committee vote. Recession odds are colour only.

base.story: WFE grows about 22% in 2027 to about $175B (SEMI) or more (sell-side $180-213B), led by DRAM/HBM and leading-edge logic. Lam delivers FY27 EPS of about $9.5, with FY28 visible at about $11.9. The forward multiple slips from about 28x FY28 to about 26-28x NTM as the market looks toward slower 2028 growth. Earnings growth slightly outruns de-rating, so the stock ends near to slightly above today.

bull.story: The sell-side supercycle plays out (GS: WFE $218B in 2027 and $281B in 2028). 3D DRAM, NAND upgrades and GAA/backside power give Lam share gains in etch and deposition. FY28 EPS reaches about $14.5-15, the multiple holds at about 33x because 2029 also looks like a growth year, and the stock clears the $438.50 June high.

thesis_break_reason: About 18x my FY28 EPS ($11.9) and 18x the FY28 consensus ($11.74), about 22.5x FY27. That is a third below today, under the Jul 29 capitulation close ($252) and the Sep 16-17 closing lows ($269). The AI-sentiment shocks of July and September both held above $250. A trade at $215 would mean the market is pricing an actual 2028 WFE decline (a memory or TSMC capex cut, or the AI build-out pause turning into order push-outs) or a major new China rule, not ordinary volatility. Historically this is where a pre-peak de-rating to high-teens multiples lands.

reasoning: Reported basics come from Lam's Q4 FY26 release: FY26 revenue of $23.2B; a Sep-quarter guide of $8.1B and $2.15 EPS; China at 26% of June-quarter revenue. S&P Global consensus is $9.51 for FY27 and $11.74 for FY28. At $324 the stock trades about 34x FY27 and 28x FY28. Round 2 accepts the supervisor's findings. SEMI's July 14, 2026 mid-year forecast (verified: WFE $143.9B in 2026, +21.8% in 2027, +14.1% in 2028) is now my independent industry anchor in place of the JPM/GS secondary copies, so my FY28 inputs move slightly down ($12.0 to $11.9 EPS; $42B to $41.5B revenue). The August move was +10% from Aug 3, not +29% (that was from the Jul 29 $252 low). The Polymarket 35% recession figure is unverified (the page did not render any market data again), so it no longer sizes the bear weight. The report date is an estimate. The supervisor asked for a dated base rate on the multiple before past WFE peaks. Year-end trailing P/E fell from 15.9x to 6.8x into the 2018-19 downturn, from 21.3x to 11.0x in 2022, and from 29.7x to 21.7x in 2024. So semicap de-rates by roughly a third to a half in the year the market starts to see a peak, even while earnings are still near highs. The open question for Sep 2027 is whether the market sees 2028 as the peak. SEMI forecasts growth, but a slowdown from +22% to +14% is exactly the second-derivative turn that preceded past de-ratings. I therefore keep a modest de-rating (26x) in the base case and put the historical-style collapse to about 18x in a 23% bear case. Fair value is about $304 (P/E $309, FCF $298). Earnings growth roughly offsets de-rating, so the 12-month median is about $322, slightly below spot. Right skew from the bull case lifts the mean to about $340. Dispersion is lognormal with sigma about 0.50, not the 65% realized, which is inflated by the 152% run. It sits between semicap's long-run 45-50% and recent realized. The left tail is fattened slightly for the 40-55% cycle drawdowns. The net ladder change from round 1 is small: P(>=324) goes from 0.485 to 0.494, with slightly higher odds in the middle, because the earnings path is firmer (SEMI, consensus) and recession odds are downweighted, partly offset by the new de-rating base rate. Where I differ from the supervisor: its $310 fair value uses 26.5x on $11.7 and a 92% NI-to-FCF conversion. I stay at about $304 because the pre-peak de-rating base rate argues against paying more than about 26x, and because capex for the cleanroom-constrained build-out should keep FCF conversion below 92%.
